name: Davco Ceramacrete
paste:
DAVCO CERAMACRETE: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: Davco Ceramacrete, September 2022, Version 01.01 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/v/davco-ceramacrete.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide Davco Ceramacrete where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (September 2022, Version 01.01).
1.2 Product description. A cement based tile adhesive for ridged substrates equipped with patented DUST LESS technology that reduces airborne dust by up to 80% in the mixing phase.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer.
    - Suitable for interior and exterior applications. Domestic and light duty commercial walls and floors including bathrooms, showers, kitchens, laundries, living rooms, balconies and patios.
    - When mixed with Davco Davelastic, Davco Ceramacrete is suitable for flexible framed substrates.
1.4 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer - Suitable tile types include.
    - Ceramic,
    - Mosaic,
    - Terracotta,
    - Slate
    - Quarry tiles
    - Concrete
    - Cement based screeds and renders
    - Rendered block or brickwork.
    Not suitable for Natural stone
    Suitable substrates include:
1.5 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.9.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. Davco Ceramacrete
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Approvals, certificates and standards stated by the manufacturer. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (September 2022, Version 01.01) has no approvals, certificates or standards section.
2.3 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - SCAQMD method 304-91: cited with a stated property or value. Where: Product Information > Volatile organic compound (VOC) content (p.1).
    - AS3958.1: referred to in instructions or limitations. Where: Further Information (p.2).
2.4 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Dustless formula for less mess, less dust and fast clean up
    - Use for thin or thick bed tiling
    - Good bond strength
    - Colour varies from white to grey
2.5 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Volatile organic compound (VOC) content: Low VOC - 5g/L (SCAQMD method 304-91)
2.6 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Packaging: 5kg Plastic Bags; 20kg Paper Bags
    - Shelf life: Paper bags: If unopened 12 months from date of manufacture. Plastic film bags: If unopened 18 months from date of manufacture.
    - Storage conditions: Store in an elevated cool dry location out of direct sunlight.

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (September 2022, Version 01.01) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Substrate quality.
    - All surfaces must be installed according to manufacturer’s instructions and relevant Australian Standard(s) and be structurally sound, dry, clean and free from movement, oil, grease, wax, sealers, curing compounds, release agents and any other loose or contaminating material. Thoroughly clean old surfaces, or new surfaces that have been treated, prior to tiling.
    - Deeply contaminated surfaces must be scabbled / abraded to a clean, sound surface. Expose at least 80% of the original substrate of painted surfaces.
3.3 Substrate preparation - Priming Guide.
    | Substrate | Specific requirement | Priming |
    | Concrete - wood float finish | Cured a min 6 weeks | Prime with Davco PrimeX or Ultraprime |
    | Concrete - steel trowel finish | Cured min 6 weeks and free | Prime with Davco PrimeX |
    | (smooth) | of Laitance (not flaking) |
    | Rendered Brick or blockwork | Cured min 7 days (sound , not drummy or cracked) | Prime with Davco PrimeX or Ultraprime |
    | Screed - wood float finish | Cured min 7 days (sound, not drummy or cracked) | Prime with Davco PrimeX or Ultraprime |
    | Existing ceramic tiles (provided tile is not sealed) | Securely bonded existing tiles (not drummy) | Prime with Davco Ultrabond or Sika Prep n Prime |
    | Other difficult / non absorbent substrates (e.g. contaminated / old flooring adhesive or tile adhesive) | Where not feasible to remove | Prime with Davco Ultrabond or Sika Prep n Prime |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
    Refer to the primer product datasheet for additional information.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (September 2022, Version 01.01) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Consumption: A 20Kg Bag with cover approximately 6-7 m² with a 6mm notched trowel.
    - Pot Life: 40 Minutes
    - Open Time: 7 minutes
    - Adjustability Time: 15 Minutes
4.3 Mixing Ratio. 5kg bag: 1.25 Litre of clean cool water; 20Kg bag: 5 Litres of clean cool water; For flexible / framed substrates or submerged applications such as pools and spas the water ratio shall be diluted 1:1 with Davco Davelastic additive.
4.4 Applied Product Ready for Use.
    | Application | Wait time |
    | Prior to grouting | 24 hours |
    | Return to dry area service | 24 hours |
    | Return to wet area service | 7 days |
    | All measurements are taken at 23ºC and 50% relative humidity. Specifications vary according to site conditions and should be taken as a guide only |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
4.5 Equipment.
    - Personal protective equipment
    - Mixing drill with stirrer attachment
    - Notched trowel
    - Mixing buckets
    - Select a trowel with an appropriate square-notch size for the size and type of tile, as per the following:
    | Tile size | Notched trowel size | Back buttering required |
    | Mosaic | 4 to 6mm | - |
    | 150x150mm | 6mm | - |
    | 200x200mm | 8mm | - |
    | 250x250mm | 8mm | - |
    | 300x300mm | 10mm | - |
    | 400x400 and larger | 12mm | Yes |
    | Tiles with lugs or uneven backs | as above dependant on size | Yes |
    | Translucent tiles | as above dependant on size | Yes |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
4.6 Mixing.
    - 1. Measure the right amount of clean, potable water into a clean bucket. 2. Slowly add the powder into the water while mixing with a mixing paddle attached to a drill. Do not mix by hand. 3. Continue to mix for several minutes until a creamy consistency is achieved, free of lumps of powder. 4. Allow mixture to stand for 5 minutes, remix then use the adhesive.
    - Davco Ceramacrete may require to be remixed during its pot life, do not add additional water.
4.7 Application - Laying the Tiles. 1. Deposit a quantity of adhesive onto the prepared substrate. Do not apply more adhesive than can be tiled within the open time of the product, usually from a single tile up to around 1m2 at a time. 2. Hold the notched trowel at an angle of 60º or greater to the substrate 3. Spread the adhesive over the area where tile is to be applied, forming straight rows of adhesive “beads”. 4. Where “back buttering” is required, use the straight side of the trowel to apply a thin covering of adhesive to the back of the tile. 5. Position the tile on the beaded adhesive and press firmly. 6. Move the tile forward and then back at 90º across the direction of the beads to ensure all beads are flattened leaving no voids under the tile. Occasionally lift a tile after placing it to check that the beads are fully compressed, and that sufficient coverage has been achieved (90-100%). Replace the tile. 7. After laying a section at a time, remove any excess adhesive from the surface of the tiles and within the grout joint while the adhesive is still wet.
    - Allow product to set before grouting
    - Allow product to set firmly before return to service
    Note: Setting times of adhesive is affected by site conditions, climate and could be faster or slower than specified
4.8 Cleaning of tools.
    - Clean tools and equipment with water before the adhesive dries.
4.9 Limitations and important considerations.
    - Test product in an inconspicuous area first
    - Do not apply in temperatures above 35ºC or below 5ºC
    - In cool and / or humid conditions, allow longer setting times
    - Do not allow the adhesive to skin prior to laying the tiles. If the adhesive skins remove and dispose of it, then re-apply fresh adhesive
    - For flexible substrates use with Davco Davelastic additive.
    - Seek Sika written specification for submerged applications such as pools and spas.
    - For other uses not mentioned in these instructions, please contact Sika Australia
4.10 Further information. It is essential to plan the area to be tiled, with inclusion of movement joints, in accordance with the Australian Standard AS3958.1 “Guide to the Installation of Ceramic Tiles.” Failure to do so may result in drummy or lifting tiles. Make sure normal building or surface movement is accommodated by installing movement joints as follows:
    - Over movement joints in the substrate
    - At a junction between different substrate materials
    - At fixtures interrupting the tile surface e.g. columns
    - At internal vertical corners
    - Around the perimeter of the tiling system
    - At a maximum of 4.5m centres, in a grid pattern
    Movement joints should be kept free from dirt and adhesive droppings.
    All movement joints can be filled with Davco Elite Silicone or a Sika flexible Sealant.

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Conditions stated in the limitations. Also stated in the data sheet limitations (clause 4.9):
    - Do not apply in temperatures above 35ºC or below 5ºC
5.3 Trials, test areas and compatibility checks stated by the manufacturer.
    - Test product in an inconspicuous area first
5.4 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.5 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: Davco Ceramacrete, September 2022, Version 01.01, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/v/davco-ceramacrete.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: Davco Ceramacrete, version 09/04/2025, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/d/MSDS%20Davco%20Ceramacrete%20GHS7.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS Davco Ceramacrete, version 31/10/2025, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/x/sds-davco-ceramacrete.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS Powder 210, version 31/10/2025, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/w/sds-powder-210.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety related data.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
